title: Gluing quasi-compact open immersions above an affine base cover
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ and $\pi:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $\pi$ affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $S=\bigcup_{a\in A}S_a$ be an affine open cover. Put $Z_a=h^{-1}(S_a)$ and $Y_a=\pi^{-1}(S_a)$, and write $\iota_a:Y_a\hookrightarrow Y$ for the open inclusion. Suppose every $Z_a$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and for every $a$ there is an open immersion $e_a:Z_a\to Y_a$ [def-weil-open-immersion] over $S_a$, meaning $(\pi|_{Y_a})\circ e_a=h|_{Z_a}$ as morphisms to $S_a$. Suppose that for all $a,b$ the restrictions of $\iota_a\circ e_a$ and $\iota_b\circ e_b$ to $Z_a\cap Z_b$ are equal as morphisms into $Y$. Then there is a unique morphism $c:Z\to Y$ restricting to $\iota_a\circ e_a$ on each $Z_a$. It satisfies $\pi\circ c=h$ and is a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion]. No injectivity of a pre-existing global map, finiteness of the cover, quasi-compactness or separation of $S$, or quasi-separatedness of $h$ is assumed; an empty cover is allowed.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, proof of (2) implies (4), final gluing and quasi-compact-open-immersion assertion

proof.text: The opens $Z_a=h^{-1}(S_a)$ cover $Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to the compatible morphisms $\iota_a\circ e_a:Z_a\to Y$. This gives the unique morphism $c:Z\to Y$ with the required restrictions. The compatibility hypothesis is exactly equality into $Y$ on each overlap; no assertion that an overlap is affine is needed.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, proof (2) implies (4), final local-to-global assertion; expanded using Schemes Tags 01JB, 01K4 and 03GI

proof.text: On $Z_a$, the equality $\pi\circ c=h$ is the given equality over $S_a$, followed by $S_a\hookrightarrow S$. The equality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] therefore gives $\pi\circ c=h$ globally. Consequently $c^{-1}(Y_a)=c^{-1}(\pi^{-1}(S_a))=h^{-1}(S_a)=Z_a$ as open subschemes, and the restriction $Z_a\to Y_a$ is $e_a$.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, proof (2) implies (4), final local-to-global assertion; expanded using Schemes Tags 01JB, 01K4 and 03GI

proof.text: If $c(z)=c(z\prime)=y$, choose $a$ with $\pi(y)\in S_a$. The previous equality places both points in $Z_a$, where injectivity of $e_a$ gives $z=z\prime$. Each composite $Z_a\xrightarrow{e_a}Y_a\xrightarrow{\iota_a}Y$ is an open immersion: by [def-weil-open-immersion] it is the composite of isomorphisms onto open subschemes, whose image remains open in $Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-injective-local-source] to $c$ and the covering inclusions $Z_a\hookrightarrow Z$. Its injectivity and local open-immersion hypotheses have just been verified, so $c$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, proof (2) implies (4), final local-to-global assertion; expanded using Schemes Tags 01JB, 01K4 and 03GI

proof.text: By the definition [pqf-def-affine-morphism], $Y_a=\pi^{-1}(S_a)$ is affine. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] makes $Y_a$ quasi-separated. The assumed quasi-compactness of $Z_a$ and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied to $e_a:Z_a\to Y_a$, show that $e_a$ is quasi-compact. This uses quasi-separatedness of the affine target chart, not of $h$ or $S$.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, proof (2) implies (4), final local-to-global assertion; expanded using Schemes Tags 01JB, 01K4 and 03GI

proof.text: The opens $Y_a$ cover $Y$, and the restrictions $c^{-1}(Y_a)\to Y_a$ are precisely the quasi-compact maps $e_a$. By [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target], $c$ is quasi-compact. Together with step 3 this proves the assertion. If $A$ is empty, its covering property forces $S$, hence $Z$ and $Y$, to be empty; the same gluing, injectivity and target-cover arguments apply vacuously.

Source: Stacks morphisms.tex 01SM lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2)=>(4), whose last sentence 'Thus can is a quasi-compact open immersion' is the omitted local-to-global step that the split supplies (D5). Step checks: 1, the morphisms are glued from overlap equality into Y, with no affine overlaps needed. 2, pi∘c = h holds chartwise and then globally by the equality clause, so c^{-1}(Y_a) = Z_a and the restriction is e_a because iota_a is a monomorphism. 3, c is injective: equal images force h(z) = h(z') in some S_a, and the source-local open-immersion criterion applies to the covering inclusions Z_a into Z. 4, Y_a is affine by the definition of affine, hence quasi-separated, and Z_a is quasi-compact, so e_a is quasi-compact by permanence (1). 5, quasi-compactness is local on the target cover Y_a. Edge cases checked: empty cover, empty Z_a, infinite cover, non-quasi-compact or non-separated S, and the non-Noetherian case. The quasi-compactness of Z_a is needed, since a punctured A^infinity is not quasi-compact. Duplicate check: lem-trf-canonical-affine-charts-qc-open-immersion (sk-i-curve-zero) assumes a given global map and canonical charts; it is not a duplicate and is off-route. The item cites no SGA source. The item's conclusions match what the parent lem-a1-quasi-affine-target-locality step 4 uses.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unique_quasiCompact_isOpenImmersion_of_affine_base_cover {Z Y S : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ S) (π : Y ⟶ S) [IsAffineHom π] {A : Type v} (U : A → S.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤) (hUa : ∀ a : A, IsAffineOpen (U a)) (hZ : ∀ a : A, CompactSpace (h ⁻¹ᵁ U a).toScheme) (e : ∀ a : A, (h ⁻¹ᵁ U a).toScheme ⟶ (π ⁻¹ᵁ U a).toScheme) (he : ∀ a : A, IsOpenImmersion (e a)) (heS : ∀ a : A, e a ≫ (π ∣_ U a) = h ∣_ U a) (heq : ∀ a b : A, Z.homOfLE (inf_le_left : h ⁻¹ᵁ U a ⊓ h ⁻¹ᵁ U b ≤ h ⁻¹ᵁ U a) ≫ e a ≫ (π ⁻¹ᵁ U a).ι = Z.homOfLE (inf_le_right : h ⁻¹ᵁ U a ⊓ h ⁻¹ᵁ U b ≤ h ⁻¹ᵁ U b) ≫ e b ≫ (π ⁻¹ᵁ U b).ι) : ∃ c : Z ⟶ Y, (∀ a : A, (h ⁻¹ᵁ U a).ι ≫ c = e a ≫ (π ⁻¹ᵁ U a).ι) ∧ c ≫ π = h ∧ QuasiCompact c ∧ IsOpenImmersion c ∧ ∀ c' : Z ⟶ Y, (∀ a : A, (h ⁻¹ᵁ U a).ι ≫ c' = e a ≫ (π ⁻¹ᵁ U a).ι) → c' = c
